chunks: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad said: Hakim ibn Dawud narrated to me, who narrated to me Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
He said: 'The sacred precinct (haram) of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is five farsakhs from its four sides.'

key_terms.أَرْبَعِ جَوَانِبِهِ: From its four sides; indicating the boundary extends in all directions.
key_terms.حَرِيمُ: Sacred precinct or sanctuary; a protected area where specific rules apply.
key_terms.فَرَاسِخَ: Farsakhs; a traditional unit of distance, plural of farsakh.
key_terms.قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

ai.seo_question: What is the defined boundary of the sacred precinct of Imam Husayn's grave?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the legal boundaries of the sacred precinct (haram) surrounding the tomb of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him), defining it as extending five farsakhs in all four cardinal directions. This measurement, rooted in Shia jurisprudence, underscores the spiritual and physical sanctity of Karbala, influencing the rituals of ziyarah and the status of the soil (turba) taken from the site. The specification of 'five farsakhs' reflects the traditional understanding of the area's holiness, distinguishing it as a place of divine proximity and pilgrimage.
